Project - ResumeIQ (Architecture and Workflow)

ResumeIQ is built as a stateful LangGraph pipeline with 4 nodes: extract, 
agent, tools, and analyze. When a user uploads their resume and a job 
description, the system first uses PyMuPDF to extract raw text from the PDF. 
The extract node then uses a llama-3.1-8b-instant model to parse this text 
into a structured JSON containing skills, experience, projects, and required 
and preferred skills from the JD. This structured data is stored in the 
LangGraph state and passed forward through the pipeline.

The agent node receives this structured data and makes an LLM call using the 
20b parameter model to decide which tools to invoke based on the identified 
skill gaps. The ATS keyword checker is hardcoded to always run, while the 
agent autonomously chooses whether to call the Adzuna job market API and the 
YouTube Data API based on what gaps it finds in the candidate's profile.

data, and all tool results â€” and makes a third LLM call using the 20b model 
with a structured prompt to generate a comprehensive analysis. The graph 
structure is linear: extract â†’ agent â†’ tools â†’ analyze â†’ END. Chat 
functionality is handled outside the graph, called directly from the REST API 
endpoint.

node using the 8b model, one in the agent node, and one in the analyze node 
both using the 20b model.

Project Challenges - Personal Assistant

Building the personal assistant came with several 
interesting challenges. The first was deciding how 
to write and structure the personal data so it 
could be chunked properly for accurate retrieval. 
Anshu learned that natural conversational language 
retrieves far better than bullet point lists â€” so 
instead of writing her information like a resume, 
she wrote it as answers to questions a recruiter 
might ask. The second challenge was a RAG retrieval 
domination problem â€” when querying for all projects, 
ChromaDB was only returning ResumeIQ chunks because 
ResumeIQ had 5 chunks versus one chunk for other 
projects, crowding out smaller topics in semantic 
search. She fixed this by running two separate 
targeted queries per topic and combining the results, 
learning that data distribution in a vector database 
directly affects retrieval quality.  
These challenges taught Anshu that in AI systems, 
data quality and system design matter as much as 
model choice.

Project Challenges - Building ResumeIQ

The biggest challenge Anshu faced building ResumeIQ was 
managing token limits and token usage across the pipeline 
given free tier LLM API constraints. With a resume, job 
description, and multiple tool results all being fed into 
prompts simultaneously, token usage spiked quickly and 
responses were getting cut off or degraded in quality. 
She solved this by splitting work across two models â€” 
using the smaller 8b model for the extraction node where 
structured output matters more than reasoning depth, and 
reserving the 70b model only for agent and analysis nodes 
where quality is critical. This dual model architecture 
effectively doubled the token budget while maintaining 
output quality. For chat memory she implemented a custom 
history compression function keeping the first 2 messages 
and last 10 messages, discarding the middle of long

Project - ResumeIQ (Overview)

ResumeIQ is Anshu's flagship AI project â€” a fully deployed agentic resume 
analyzer built using LangGraph. It analyzes a candidate's resume against a 
job description and provides detailed feedback including ATS score, skill gap

live and accessible at https://agentic-resume-analyzer.netlify.app/ with a

Project - Personal Assistant (ResumeIQ Integration)

The personal assistant integrates Anshu's ResumeIQ project as a live tool.

will automatically call the ResumeIQ backend API with Anshu's resume and

from YouTube â€” and returns a detailed analysis. The personal assistant then 
formats this analysis into a clean response. This makes the assistant not 
just a static Q&A system but a live demonstration of Anshu's agentic AI 
work, where two of her projects work together as an integrated system.

Project - ResumeIQ (Tool Orchestration)

ResumeIQ orchestrates 3 tools. The ATS keyword checker always runs as 
described above. The Adzuna job market API is called when the agent identifies 
skill gaps â€” it returns the number of active job listings for a skill and 
average salary data, giving the candidate a real sense of how in-demand their 
missing skills are in the current market. The YouTube Data API is called to 
find relevant learning resources for the missing skills, so the candidate gets 
actionable course recommendations directly in the analysis. The agent node 
uses an LLM call to autonomously decide which of the latter two tools to 
invoke based on the candidate's specific skill gaps.

Project - ResumeIQ (Architecture and Workflow)

ResumeIQ is built as a stateful LangGraph pipeline with 4 nodes: extract, 
agent, tools, and analyze. When a user uploads their resume and a job 
description, the system first uses PyMuPDF to extract raw text from the PDF. 
The extract node then uses a llama-3.1-8b-instant model to parse this text

and preferred skills from the JD. This structured data is stored in the 
LangGraph state and passed forward through the pipeline.

20b parameter model to decide which tools to invoke based on the identified 
skill gaps. The ATS keyword checker is hardcoded to always run, while the 
agent autonomously chooses whether to call the Adzuna job market API and the 
YouTube Data API based on what gaps it finds in the candidate's profile.

The tools node executes the decided tools and updates the state with their 
results. Finally the analyze node receives the full state â€” resume data, JD 
data, and all tool results â€” and makes a third LLM call using the 20b model 
with a structured prompt to generate a comprehensive analysis. The graph 
structure is linear: extract â†’ agent â†’ tools â†’ analyze â†’ END. Chat 
functionality is handled outside the graph, called directly from the REST API 
endpoint.

In total ResumeIQ makes 3 LLM calls per full analysis: one in the extract 
node using the 8b model, one in the agent node, and one in the analyze node 
both using the 20b model.

live and accessible at https://agentic-resume-analyzer.netlify.app/ with a 
Flask backend deployed on Render and a single-page frontend on Netlify.

described above. The Adzuna job market API is called when the agent identifies 
skill gaps â€” it returns the number of active job listings for a skill and 
average salary data, giving the candidate a real sense of how in-demand their 
missing skills are in the current market. The YouTube Data API is called to 
find relevant learning resources for the missing skills, so the candidate gets 
actionable course recommendations directly in the analysis. The agent node 
uses an LLM call to autonomously decide which of the latter two tools to 
invoke based on the candidate's specific skill gaps.

ResumeIQ is built as a stateful LangGraph pipeline with 4 nodes: extract, 
agent, tools, and analyze. When a user uploads their resume and a job 
description, the system first uses PyMuPDF to extract raw text from the PDF. 
The extract node then uses a llama-3.1-8b-instant model to parse this text

structure is linear: extract â†’ agent â†’ tools â†’ analyze â†’ END. Chat 
functionality is handled outside the graph, called directly from the REST API 
endpoint.

both using the 20b model.

question: What makes ResumeIQ technically challenging?
chunks:
Project - ResumeIQ (Future Scope)

Anshu has planned several meaningful extensions for ResumeIQ. A resume 
rewrite tool that automatically rewrites the candidate's resume to better 
match JD keywords and improve the ATS score is high on the list. An interview 
mode is also planned where the system will conduct a mock interview based on 
the resume and JD requirements, asking role-relevant questions and evaluating 
answers. A multi-resume comparison feature is also being considered, allowing 
candidates to compare two versions of their resume side by side against the 
same JD.

Project - ResumeIQ (Overview)

ResumeIQ is Anshu's flagship AI project â€” a fully deployed agentic resume 
analyzer built using LangGraph. It analyzes a candidate's resume against a 
job description and provides detailed feedback including ATS score, skill gap 
analysis, job market insights, and curated learning resources. The project is 
live and accessible at https://agentic-resume-analyzer.netlify.app/ with a 
Flask backend deployed on Render and a single-page frontend on Netlify.

Project - Personal Assistant (ResumeIQ Integration)

The personal assistant integrates Anshu's ResumeIQ project as a live tool. 
Recruiters can paste a job description directly into the assistant and it 
will automatically call the ResumeIQ backend API with Anshu's resume and 
the provided JD. ResumeIQ runs its full agentic LangGraph pipeline â€” ATS 
keyword analysis, job market data from Adzuna, and course recommendations 
from YouTube â€” and returns a detailed analysis. The personal assistant then 
formats this analysis into a clean response. This makes the assistant not 
just a static Q&A system but a live demonstration of Anshu's agentic AI 
work, where two of her projects work together as an integrated system.

Project - ResumeIQ (ATS Keyword Checker)

The ATS keyword checker is a custom Python function Anshu built from scratch. 
It computes a keyword match percentage between the resume and job description 
using set intersection â€” finding matched keywords as the intersection of JD 
words and resume words, and missing keywords as the difference. The match 
percentage is calculated as the number of matched keywords divided by total JD 
keywords multiplied by 100. It also checks resume formatting by verifying 
whether standard sections like skills, education, projects, and experience 
exist in the resume, and flags any missing sections as formatting issues. The 
function returns the match percentage, top matched and missing keywords, 
formatting issues, and an overall ATS pass or fail based on whether the match 
percentage is above 60 percent and there are no formatting issues.

Project - ResumeIQ (Architecture and Workflow)

ResumeIQ is built as a stateful LangGraph pipeline with 4 nodes: extract, 
agent, tools, and analyze. When a user uploads their resume and a job 
description, the system first uses PyMuPDF to extract raw text from the PDF. 
The extract node then uses a llama-3.1-8b-instant model to parse this text 
into a structured JSON containing skills, experience, projects, and required 
and preferred skills from the JD. This structured data is stored in the 
LangGraph state and passed forward through the pipeline.

The agent node receives this structured data and makes an LLM call using the 
20b parameter model to decide which tools to invoke based on the identified 
skill gaps. The ATS keyword checker is hardcoded to always run, while the 
agent autonomously chooses whether to call the Adzuna job market API and the 
YouTube Data API based on what gaps it finds in the candidate's profile.

The tools node executes the decided tools and updates the state with their 
results. Finally the analyze node receives the full state â€” resume data, JD 
data, and all tool results â€” and makes a third LLM call using the 20b model 
with a structured prompt to generate a comprehensive analysis. The graph 
structure is linear: extract â†’ agent â†’ tools â†’ analyze â†’ END. Chat 
functionality is handled outside the graph, called directly from the REST API 
endpoint.

In total ResumeIQ makes 3 LLM calls per full analysis: one in the extract 
node using the 8b model, one in the agent node, and one in the analyze node 
both using the 20b model.
